sq.q: \(\text{A string of length } l \text{ fixed at ends is initially at rest. Given initial velocity } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0) = kx(l-x), \text{ find } y(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{General solution: } y(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi c t}{l}.\)
\(\text{Using initial velocity: } kx(l-x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \frac{n\pi c}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)
\(\text{Express RHS as Fourier sine series: } B_n \frac{n\pi c}{l} = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l kx(l-x) \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx.\)
\(\text{Evaluate integral: } = \frac{4kl^2}{n^3\pi^3}[1-(-1)^n]. \text{ For odd } n, B_n = \frac{8kl^3}{n^4\pi^4 c}.\)

sq.q: \(\text{A string of length } l \text{ fixed at both ends is initially at rest in equilibrium. Given initial velocity } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0) = v_0 \sin\frac{3\pi x}{l}, \text{ find the displacement } y(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{Solve wave equation with conditions: } y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0, y(x,0)=0, y_t(x,0)=v_0 \sin(3\pi x/l).\)
\(\text{General solution: } y(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi c t}{l}.\)
\(\text{Using initial velocity: } v_0 \sin\frac{3\pi x}{l} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \frac{n\pi c}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)
\(\text{Equate coefficients: } B_3 \frac{3\pi c}{l} = v_0 \Rightarrow B_3 = \frac{l v_0}{3\pi c}, \text{ other } B_n=0.\)
\(\text{Hence } y(x,t) = \frac{l v_0}{3\pi c} \sin\frac{3\pi x}{l} \sin\frac{3\pi c t}{l}.\)

lq.q: \(\text{A string of length } \pi \text{ is fixed at both ends. It is given an initial displacement y(x,0)=0}\\ \text{and an initial velocity \(\frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0) = x(\pi - x).\)}\\ \text{Find the displacement \( y(x,t).\)}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{Wave equation: \(y_{tt} = c^2 y_{xx}\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Initial conditions: \(y(x,0)=0\), \(y_t(x,0)=x(\pi-x).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \sin(nx)\left[C_n \cos(nct)+D_n \sin(nct)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Apply \(y(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_n=0\) for all \(n\).}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin(nx) \sin(nct).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Then \(y_t(x,t)= \sum D_n nc \sin(nx) \cos(nct).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{At \(t=0\): \(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n nc \sin(nx) = x(\pi-x).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Expand \(x(\pi-x)\) in Fourier sine series on \((0,\pi)\): \(x(\pi-x)= \sum b_n \sin(nx),\) where \(b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi} x(\pi-x) \sin(nx) dx.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Compute \(b_n\): integration by parts gives \(b_n = \dfrac{4}{\pi n^3}[1-(-1)^n].\) So \(b_n = \dfrac{8}{\pi n^3}\) for \(n\) odd, \(0\) for \(n\) even.}\) (3 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(D_n nc = b_n\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n = \dfrac{b_n}{nc}.\) For \(n\) odd: \(D_n = \dfrac{8}{\pi n^4 c}.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Final: \(y(x,t)= \sum\limits_{n \text{ odd}} \dfrac{8}{\pi n^4 c} \sin(nx) \sin(nct).\)}\) (1 Mark)
